transcript.text: Our brand new AEG FSE52407Z dishwasher keeps opening its own door a few inches near the end of the programme. Is the catch faulty? It's only 2 weeks old.

It is unlikely to be a faulty catch if the appliance is only two weeks old and under warranty; you should contact AEG for a repair or replacement rather than attempting fixes yourself. However, before doing that, we need to distinguish between a defect and normal behaviour. Some dishwashers with condensation drying will pop open slightly at the end of the cycle as steam escapes. Does water leak out onto your floor when this happens, or is it just dry? Also, does it happen on every wash?
No leaks, it's dry, just a puff of steam when it opens. Yes, it happens every wash, always near the end of the cycle.

[Heading: Probably normal]
That sounds like normal behaviour for a condensation-drying dishwasher. Many modern machines are designed to pop the door open slightly at the end of the cycle to let steam escape and help dishes dry faster, especially plastics. Since it is dry and happens consistently near the end, this is likely an intentional feature rather than a faulty catch. However, as your AEG is only two weeks old, I recommend contacting their customer support or the retailer you bought it from. They can confirm that this specific model (FSE52407Z) has this 'AutoOpen' or similar drying function and reassure you that it is not a defect under warranty.

candidates.cause: Door seal or latch mechanism issue (misalignment or defect)
Normal condensation drying behaviour (door popping slightly open due to steam pressure release)
